increments.title: The collector accepts, keeps, persists, serves and announces a run's state
increments.goal: Give the collector an endpoint of its own that accepts a run's backlog state, keep the latest state per run, serve the runs it holds and the full state of one over its JSON API behind the existing authentication, persist it across a restart, and announce every write on the existing SSE stream.
criteria: A POST of a run's state to an endpoint of the collector's own is accepted and identified by the issue the state belongs to; a second POST for the same run replaces what was held for it, so the collector keeps the latest state per run and no history.

The JSON API answers both questions: the runs the collector holds, with what a reader needs to pick one including when each was last written, and the full state of one named run; asking for a run it does not hold answers 404.
The new ingest endpoint and the new read endpoints sit behind the collector's existing authentication and reject an unauthenticated caller exactly as its other endpoints do.
A collector restarted against the same measurement directory still serves the run state it held, persisted the way the sessions it already holds are persisted.
A write to a run's state puts a frame on the existing /api/stream SSE stream that tells an already-connected client which run changed.

tools/argus/README.md documents what the collector now accepts and serves, and tools/argus/test/CLAUDE.md and tools/argus/CLAUDE.md are current for the cases and modules this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.

increments.title: The recorder pushes the state it just wrote, best-effort and invisible
increments.goal: Make the recorder send the run's state to the configured collector after every write it makes, without changing anything an agent or a workflow sees and without ever costing a run a failure, a wait or a line of output.
criteria: init, record, branch and close each send the state they just wrote to the collector's run-state endpoint, identified by the issue the state belongs to, so a collector that receives it then serves that exact document under that issue.
The recorder stays the only writer of backlog.json and keeps its zero dependencies; no agent page and no workflow prompt changes, so how an agent calls the recorder is exactly what it is today.
The collector's address and its credential are read from the same OTLP collector environment the rest of uroboros already exports for argus, and from nowhere else.
With no collector configured in the environment, the recorder does nothing extra.

A collector that is unreachable, slow or refusing costs the recorder neither a non-zero exit nor a wait beyond a short timeout, and produces no output: the exit codes and the one confirmation line of every subcommand stay byte-identical to today's.
skills/agent-brief/assets/CLAUDE.md is current for the cases and helpers this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.
node --test skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs exits 0 and ./test.sh exits 0.

Verified on Node 20, 21 and 22. No agent page, workflow prompt or argus file changed. Merged into claude/argus-workflow-backlog-status-nvqmvr.

increments.title: argus-ui gains a run view: one run's backlog, switchable and live
increments.goal: Give the interface a run view beside its session view that shows a run's backlog as the collector serves it, opens on the most recently written run, lets the reader switch runs, and updates itself over the collector's SSE stream.
criteria: The interface shows a run view beside its existing session view, holding for the run it shows: the issue and the workflow it belongs to and when it was last written; the increments in the backlog's order, each with its id, title, status, branch and note; a count of how many increments are closed and how many are open; and the codemap.
A closed increment reads as closed, with its status and its note.

The view opens on the run written to most recently and the reader can switch to any other run the collector holds, taking both the list of runs and the one run's whole state from the collector's run endpoints and from no other source.

A write to the shown run's state reaches an already-open page live over the collector's Server-Sent-Events stream, whose frame names only which run changed and when: no polling, no reload, no manual refresh.
The existing session view, its timeline and its stream handling keep working unchanged beside the new view.
argus-ui still imports nothing outside itself and reads no uroboros file; test/independence.test.mjs still guards exactly that rule, covers every module this increment adds, and passes.

tools/argus-ui/README.md says what the interface now shows, and tools/argus-ui/test/CLAUDE.md and tools/argus-ui/CLAUDE.md are current for the cases and modules this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.

## What gets built A run view beside the session view in argus-ui: a second sidebar listing the runs the collector holds, a second detail pane showing one run's backlog, a switch between the two views, and a live reload driven by the collector's `run` SSE frame. No file under `tools/argus` is touched; argus-ui reads run state only over `/api/runs` and `/api/runs/:id`, which its own proxy already forwards. ## The wire contract you build against (verified in the collector's source) - `GET /api/runs` answers `{ total, items }`. Each item is `{ id, issue, workflow, increments, updatedAtMs }` — `increments` here is a NUMBER (the count), and there is no `state`. The list is latest-write-first, so `items[0]` is the run written to most recently. - `GET /api/runs/:id` answers one entry whole: `{ id, issue, workflow, increments: , updatedAtMs, state: }`, or 404 `{ error: 'unknown run' }`. - The `state` document is the backlog file as the recorder writes it: `{ version, issue, workflow, codemap, increments: [ { id, title, goal, criteria, status, note, branch, steps } ], run: { steps: [...] } }`. `status` is `'todo'` until a close, then one of `'done' | 'blocked' | 'dropped'`; `note` and `branch` are `''` when unset; `close` empties `steps`. - **The sharp edge**: the entry's `increments` is a count, the document's `state.increments` is the array. Read every increment, and both counts, from `run.state.increments`; `run.increments.map(...)` is a crash. - The SSE stream: `event: run` with `data: {"id":"…","updatedAtMs":123}`, sent uncoalesced and immediately, alongside the existing `hello` and `ingest` events. The frame carries no state, so the handler has to fetch. - The collector holds the document opaquely, so treat every field as possibly absent: a missing `codemap`, a missing `increments` array or a `state` that is not the shape above must render a head and a placeholder, never a crash and never the strings `undefined` or `NaN`. ## New module: public/run.js Named `run.js` (suite `test/run.test.mjs`), beside `timeline.js` and `context.js` and following their rule exactly: pure functions returning HTML strings, no browser global — no `document.`, no `fetch(`, no `location.` — because `independence.test.mjs` scans for those three patterns and the suite imports the module directly into `node --test`. It imports `esc` and `fmtAgo` from `./format.js` and nothing else. Exports: - `CLOSED_STATUSES` — `new Set(['done', 'blocked', 'dropped'])`, the three statuses the recorder's `close` writes. Anything else, `'todo'` and `''` included, is open. - `isClosedIncrement(increment)` — membership in that set. - `incrementCounts(increments)` — `{ total, closed, open }` over the document's array, tolerating a non-array by counting zero. - `pickRunId(items, wanted)` — the run to show: `wanted` when the list holds it, else `items[0]?.id`, else `null`. This is the whole of "opens on the run written to most recently": the collector already sorts latest-write-first, so the page sorts nothing. - `runFrame(data)` — parse one SSE `run` frame's `data` string to `{ id, updatedAtMs }`, or `null` for malformed JSON, a non-object or a missing id. A bad frame must cost nothing. - `renderRunList({ items, selectedId })` — the picker's `

Named so it does not shadow the imported `renderRunList`. - `renderRunView()` — writes `renderRun(state.run)` into `#run-detail`. - `loadRuns()` — `api('/api/runs')`, sets `state.runs`, then `state.selectedRunId = pickRunId(state.runs, state.selectedRunId)`. - `loadRun()` — with no selection, `state.run = null`; else `api(\`/api/runs/\${encodeURIComponent(id)}\`)` into `state.run`, guarded by the same stale-answer check the timeline loader uses (`if (state.selectedRunId !== id) return;`) and swallowing a failure into `state.run = null` rather than throwing past the render. - `refreshRuns(changedId = null)` — `await loadRuns()`; reload the shown run when `changedId` is null (boot and explicit switch) or equals `state.selectedRunId`, or when nothing was selected before; then `renderRunPicker()` and `renderRunView()`. ## A. test/run.test.mjs — NEW FILE, unit, `node --test` importing `../public/run.js`

Command that runs just it: `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/run.test.mjs`

Fixtures, file-local, each taking an `over` object spread last, in the style of `context.test.mjs`:

- `increment(over)` → `{ id: 'ui', title: 'the run view', goal: '', criteria: [], status: 'todo', note: '', branch: '', steps: [] }`
- `doc(over)` → the backlog document: `{ version: 1, issue: 'docs/issues/2026-08-08-x', workflow: 'agile-loop', codemap: 'a.js — a.\nb.js — b.', increments: [increment()], run: { steps: [] } }`
- `runEntry(over)` → the one-run answer: `{ id: 'docs/issues/2026-08-08-x', issue: 'docs/issues/2026-08-08-x', workflow: 'agile-loop', increments: 1, updatedAtMs: Date.now() - 5000, state: doc() }`
- `listItem(over)` → a `/api/runs` item: `runEntry` without `state`.

Cases:

**Criterion 1 — what the run view holds.**
1. `renderRun(runEntry())` names the issue, the workflow and when the run was last written: the markup contains the issue text, the workflow text, the `fmtAgo` string for `updatedAtMs`, and `data-updated="<the ISO string of updatedAtMs>"`. Assert the ISO attribute rather than a locale-formatted date, so the case does not depend on the machine's locale.
2. One card per increment, in the document's order, each carrying its id, title, status, branch and note. Input: three increments with distinct ids `a`, `b`, `c`, the second one `{ status: 'done', note: 'accepted', branch: 'claude/x--b' }`. Assert each field's text is present and that `indexOf('a') < indexOf('b') < indexOf('c')` in the markup, so "the backlog's order" is proved rather than assumed.
3. The counts. Input: increments with statuses `done`, `blocked`, `todo`, `''`. Expected: closed 2, open 2, both rendered, and the two summing to the number of increments.
4. The codemap is rendered whole. Input: a codemap with two lines and an `&`. Expected: both lines present, the `&` escaped as `&`.
5. Everything is escaped: an increment title of `<script>alert(1)</script>`, a note containing `"` and `'`, an issue containing `<`. Expected: no raw `<script` in the markup.
6. `renderRun(null)` renders a placeholder that says no run state is held, and no increment card. Edge: this is what an empty collector looks like.
7. The increments come from `state.increments` and never from the entry's count. Input: `runEntry({ increments: 99, state: doc({ increments: [increment({id:'a'}), increment({id:'b'})] }) })`. Expected: two cards, and the markup does not print `99`. This is the shape trap; the case exists to pin it.
8. Edge — an opaque document: `runEntry({ state: { issue: 'i' } })` (no `increments`, no `codemap`, no `workflow`) renders the head and a placeholder in place of the increments, and the markup contains neither `undefined` nor `NaN`.
9. Edge — `runEntry({ state: doc({ increments: [] }) })`: zero closed, zero open, a placeholder instead of an empty block.

**Criterion 2 — a closed increment reads as closed.**
10. `isClosedIncrement`: `done`, `blocked` and `dropped` are closed; `todo`, `''` and an unknown status are open. Assert all six, and assert `CLOSED_STATUSES` holds exactly those three — they are the recorder's, and a fourth invented here would silently miscount every run.
11. `incrementCounts`: over the four-status fixture, `{ total: 4, closed: 2, open: 2 }`; over `[]`, `{ total: 0, closed: 0, open: 0 }`; over `undefined`, the same zeroes rather than a throw.
12. A closed increment's card is marked closed and shows its status and its note; an open one carries neither the mark nor a note element. Input: one `{ status: 'done', note: 'accepted at round 0' }` and one `{ status: 'todo', note: '' }`. Expected: `data-closed="true"` on the first card only, the word `done` and the note text inside it.
13. Edge — a closed increment with an empty note still reads as closed: `{ status: 'dropped', note: '' }` renders the closed mark and the status, and prints no empty note element and no `undefined`.
14. Edge — an increment with an empty branch renders no branch label at all, so the card does not show a dangling "branch" with nothing after it.

**Criterion 3 — opening on the latest run, and switching.**
15. `pickRunId`: `([], null)` → `null`; `([a, b], null)` → `'a'` (the collector serves latest-write-first, so the first item is the most recently written); `([a, b], 'b')` → `'b'`; `([a, b], 'gone')` → `'a'` — a run the collector no longer holds falls back to the latest rather than showing nothing.
16. `renderRunList({ items: [a, b], selectedId: 'b' })`: one button per run with `data-run` carrying that run's id, `aria-current="true"` on `b` and `aria-current="false"` on `a`, and each row showing the run's issue and its `fmtAgo` time.
17. `renderRunList({ items: [] })` renders a placeholder row, not an empty string. Edge: the same empty case the session list already handles.
18. `renderRunList` escapes the id and the issue: an id containing `"` does not break out of the `data-run` attribute.

**Criterion 4 — the SSE frame.**
19. `runFrame('{"id":"docs/issues/x","updatedAtMs":1712}')` → `{ id: 'docs/issues/x', updatedAtMs: 1712 }`. This is the collector's frame verbatim.
20. Edge — `runFrame` of `'not json'`, of `'{}'` (no id), of `'null'` and of `''` each return `null`, so a malformed frame costs the page nothing.

---

## B. test/page.test.mjs — existing file, source-text level, one new trailing section

Command that runs just it: `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/page.test.mjs`

Use the file's existing helpers — `functionSource`, `detailListener`, `callArguments`, `walk` — and add none unless a case needs one. Note `functionSource(source, 'refresh')` anchors on the literal `function refresh(`, so it will not collide with `refreshRuns`.

**Criterion 1 and 5 — the shell exists beside the session view's, which is untouched.**
21. `index.html` carries the run view's shell: `id="run-sidebar"`, `id="run-list"`, `id="run-count"`, `id="run-detail"`, a `data-view="sessions"` and a `data-view="runs"` control, and `data-view` on `<body>`. In the same case assert it still carries `id="session-list"`, `id="session-count"`, `id="detail"`, `id="session-search"` and `id="setup-modal"`, so the new shell cannot arrive by displacing the old one.
22. `app.js` imports the run module (`/from\s+['"]\.\/run\.js['"]/`) and `index.html` still loads `/app.js` as a module.

**Criterion 3 — the data comes from the run endpoints and nowhere else.**
23. `app.js` asks `/api/runs` for the list and builds the one-run path from the selected id with `encodeURIComponent`; `loadRun`'s source matches `/\/api\/runs\//` and `encodeURIComponent`. Assert too that the only network call in the run loaders is through the page's own `api(` helper — no bare `fetch(` and no second base URL — which is how "from no other source" is provable as text.
24. The state literal carries `runs: []`, `selectedRunId: null`, `run: null` and a `view:` field, sliced the way the existing state case slices it (`const state = {` to the first `\n};`).
25. `pickRunId` decides what is shown: `loadRuns`'s source calls it with `state.runs` and `state.selectedRunId`. That, plus case 15, is the whole of "opens on the most recently written run".
26. Clicking a run switches to it: the `#run-list` click listener matches `[data-run]` and calls `selectRun(`.
27. The switch is wired: a `[data-view]` click reaches `setView(`, and `setView`'s source writes `state.view` and the body's `data-view`.

**Criterion 4 — live, and not by polling.**
28. `connectStream` registers `addEventListener('run'`, its handler parses the frame with `runFrame(` and calls `refreshRuns(`; the `hello` and `ingest` listeners are still there.
29. No polling: `functionSource(appJs, 'refresh')` matches neither `/loadRuns\(/` nor `/loadRun\(/` nor `/refreshRuns\(/`; `boot`'s `setInterval` still names `renderSessionList()` and names no run function; and no `setInterval` anywhere in `app.js` names a run loader. This is the case that makes "no polling, no reload, no manual refresh" checkable.

**Criterion 5 — the session view keeps working.**
30. The run view paints only in its own containers: `renderRunPicker`'s source names `run-list` and `run-count`, `renderRunView`'s names `run-detail`, and `functionSource(appJs, 'renderDetail')` names none of the three. The existing cases already pin the `#detail` click/change/input listeners and the lane panel, so do not restate them.

**Criterion 7 — the documentation.**
31. `tools/argus-ui/README.md` describes the run view: it names the runs list, the increments with their status, and the codemap. Assert also that neither `README.md` nor `CLAUDE.md` uses the word "tab" — the existing case `no page under tools/argus-ui promises a removed view` already fails on `/\btabs?\b/i`, so do not duplicate that assertion, only the positive one.

The existing case `no class the stylesheet styles is one no source can emit` already covers the new CSS with no edit; the existing `no file under public renders a tab nav` already covers the `data-view` naming choice. Add nothing for either.

---

## C. test/independence.test.mjs — existing file, three edits, no new case

32. Criterion 6 is satisfied by adding `'public/run.js'` to all three lists: the project-completeness list in the first case, the `owned` list in the second, and `['public/context.js', 'public/timeline.js']` in the third, so the new module is checked for reaching outside the project and for touching `document.`, `fetch(` or `location.`. Keep the rule itself exactly as it is — the guard is not to be widened or relaxed.

Command: `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/independence.test.mjs`

---

## Left untested, deliberately

- **Rendering in a real browser** — clicks, `EventSource` delivery, and whether the CSS actually hides a pane. This suite has no DOM by its own convention and `app.js` is never imported; the wiring is proved as source text and the markup as strings. A DOM harness would be a dependency, which the project forbids.
- **The collector's endpoints, its persistence and its `run` frame** — owned by `tools/argus`'s suite and closed in the collector increment. Re-asserting them here would be a second implementation of someone else's contract.
- **The proxy forwarding `/api/runs`** — `server.test.mjs` already covers the `/api/` prefix and its SSE pass-through; this increment changes no proxy code.
- **Steps, their summary line and their expansion** — increment `ui-steps`.
- **The exact wording of any placeholder or heading** — the implementer's, and pinning it would fail on a better sentence.
return.summary: Add a pure public/run.js (counts, run picker, one run's backlog as HTML strings, SSE frame parsing) and wire it into index.html, app.js and styles.css as a switchable run view that reads GET /api/runs and GET /api/runs/:id, opens on the latest-written run, and reloads only on the collector's `run` SSE frame — never on a timer.

increments.title: The run view shows every step recorded, collapsed and expandable
increments.goal: Show, inside the run view, every step the backlog holds: the steps recorded against each increment and the run's own steps, each collapsed to a summary line and expandable to the full return.
criteria: Per increment the view shows the steps recorded so far, each with its label, its time and its return, collapsed to a summary line and expandable to the full return.
The run's own steps — the opening cut, each close, the publish — are shown the same way.
An increment with no steps renders as the normal state it is rather than an empty panel that looks broken, which is what a closed increment looks like once the recorder has shed its step returns.
Switching to another run, and a live write to the shown run, both leave the steps on the page matching the state now shown and no step of the state before it.
argus-ui still imports nothing outside itself and reads no uroboros file; test/independence.test.mjs covers every module this increment adds and passes.
tools/argus-ui/README.md, tools/argus-ui/test/CLAUDE.md and tools/argus-ui/CLAUDE.md are current for what this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.
npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test exits 0 and ./test.sh exits 0.
increments.note: New, split off from ui: the step returns are the one part of the run view that is its own piece of work — a return of arbitrary shape has to collapse to a line and open to the whole — and it lands on a view that already renders and updates itself.

return.summary: Landed the recorder increment's branch into claude/argus-workflow-backlog-status-nvqmvr (fast-forward e3a0cc2..b58a6b5, no conflict) and pushed it, closed `recorder` as done on the review's no-findings verdict, and re-cut the one increment still open. The change against the last cut: the single `ui` increment became two, `ui` and the new `ui-steps`. Two increments' worth of evidence made that split the right one. The collector increment fixed the wire contract (POST /api/runs, GET /api/runs latest-write-first, GET /api/runs/:id, an uncoalesced SSE frame naming only the run and its update time), and the recorder increment proved the producing half is done and untouchable, so everything left is one project's front end: a second view inside a page built for a single one, a run picker, a second kind of stream frame, and the whole shape of a backlog on screen, against an app.js of 751 lines, a page suite of 1015 and a stylesheet of 1072. That is more than one review can judge well. `ui` now takes the load-bearing half — the view exists beside the session view, shows the run's header, its increments with id, title, status, branch and note, the open/closed counts and the codemap, opens on the most recently written run, switches runs, and updates live — and `ui-steps` takes the part that is its own problem: a step return of arbitrary shape collapsing to a summary line and opening to the whole, for both an increment's steps and the run's own, plus the empty-steps state a closed increment leaves behind. Rejected: keeping `ui` whole (one review over ~2000 new lines of view, markup, styles and suites), and splitting instead into a static view and a later live one (the live path is small, and deferring it would leave the risky stream wiring for last). Issue criteria for the front end land as: the header/increments/counts/codemap clause of the big display criterion, the open-on-latest-and-switch criterion, the live-SSE criterion, the independence criterion and the closed-reads-as-closed clause in `ui`; the steps clause of the display criterion, the run's-own-steps clause and the increment-with-no-steps clause in `ui-steps`; documentation currency and a green ./test.sh sit in both, each scoped to what that increment adds. Codemap changes from this increment: the three recorder files move to the already-changed section, since the increment touched exactly them and nothing more; tools/argus-ui/public/format.js is added, hedged, because the view has times to render and format.js is where the page's formatters live; tools/argus-ui/src/config.mjs joins src/server.mjs in the deliberately-excluded list; and the exclusion of the agent pages and workflow prompts is now a fact rather than an expectation, the recorder increment having changed none of them.
